FlameLens AI | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

Building an AI powered platform to explore NASA’s microgravity combustion research and uncover insights for fire safety in space.

I’m looking for passionate collaborators in AI/ML, web development, data science, space research, and UI/UX. No expert experience required—just curiosity, creativity, and commitment!

Let’s turn space science into actionable intelligence and build something meaningful together.
summary:
Flame in Freefall is an evidence explorer containing 67 NTRS papers and two PSI reports. This gives access to a deterministic and auditable dataset. The Streamlit dashboard has filters to allow spacecraft designers, safety engineers, and researchers easily find and priorities experiments based on fuel, oxygen, pressure, inert gas, flow, gravity, geometry, and instrumentation. All numbers extracted are clearly presented with the sentences and pages they came from. An automated audit is used within the CI process so the tool fails if any quotes, values, or pages can’t be tracked back to the source.

This tool helps answer design questions such as what materials/atmospheres were investigated, what instruments were used to measure smoke and flames, how oxygen and flow affects flammability, and what gaps exist within the evidence. It also includes scenario summaries, design findings, a replay of the smoke detector using SAME data, and predictive modelling only where there is validation. This tool can help teams design safer habitats as it allows searching of decades of evidence relating to fire safety in microgravity. It also prevents duplication of experiments. This is a research tool only.
details:
Overview

Flame in Freefall is an evidence-based tool which helps microgravity combustion scientists, spacecraft fire safety engineers and mission planning personnel. It enables them to study how different factors affect combustion in microgravity. These factors include gravity, atmospheric conditions, fuel type and experimental configuration.

It takes disparate information found in scientific literature and experiments and puts it into an organised, searchable format. This helps users understand what is known through experimentation as opposed to models, assumptions or areas requiring more investigation.

1. Data Collection and Processing

This tool collects information from NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS), scientific PDFs and NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) investigation data.

In the current research there are:

  • 62 relevant research papers.
  • 57 readable documents (55 papers from NTRS, 2 reports from PSI).
  • 1,360 measurements collected with evidence.
  • 333 CFI-G experiments.
  • 7 SAME experiments.

The measurements collected have evidence to show where they originated from. This means users know where the numbers came from. The CFI-G and FLEX experiments have evidence showing where the values can be found in the original data.

2. Features

Flame in Freefall has 5 features:

A. Experimental Evidence Filter

This feature allows users to search through experimental data based on gravity, fuel type, inert gas, oxygen level, pressure, configuration and instrumentation. Users can also weight the parameters to find the most relevant research for their scenario.

B. Ask the Literature

This feature allows users to search through the research using a TF-IDF search. This allows users to find relevant sections in the literature with quotes to back up the research.

There is an optional AI enabled question answering system available . This uses the NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra. The answers given are limited to the evidence provided.

C. Flammability Evidence

This feature links the experimental conditions to relevant CFI-G measurements and FLEX droplet extinguish evidence.

The evidence from experimentation is displayed using Wilson confidence intervals. Models will only be shown if they meet the validation criteria.

One of the models tested had a validated AUC of 0.88 for the inverse flame self-extinguishing prediction using leave days out validation.

D. Design Tool and Experiment Playback

This feature plays back SAME smoke detector experiments. It has filters for the sensor data.

The data shows there was an alarm event at 923 seconds due to agreement between 2 sensors over a period of 60 seconds. This allows users to see the sensor data.

E. Scenario Summary

This feature creates a summary of the evidence for a specific atmospheric and experimental scenario. It separates information into:

  • What was measured.
  • What was modelled and validated.
  • What evidence is available.
  • What is unknown.

This is key as it shows what is unknown from experimentation.

3. Technologies and Methodology

This project used scientific document processing, organised experimental data, statistical analysis, machine learning and interactive research.

The methods used focused on:

  • Organising the evidence from scientific documents.
  • Having evidence to show where numbers originated from.
  • Comparing experiments based on the parameters.
  • Statistical analysis of the experimental data.
  • Validated modelling.
  • AI supported searching of literature with evidence.

Tools: Python 3.11, Streamlit, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, Plotly, pypdf, pydantic, Requests, openpyxl, xlrd; pytest, Ruff, Bandit, pip-audit; GitHub Actions, Streamlit Community Cloud.

This tool focuses on providing evidence based results.

4. Innovation and Relevance to NASA

The main innovation is putting together scientific documents, measurements, statistical evidence and validated modelling into an evidence based decision support tool.

Traditionally, you would have to search for the papers you needed, look through the experimental conditions, pull out the numbers and compare the results from multiple sources.

This tool helps streamline this by allowing you to search for relevant evidence.

The contract based evidence helps to show what has been measured and what has been predicted by the models. It also helps to highlight any gaps in knowledge. The models will not be shown as evidence unless they meet the validation criteria.

5. Impact

This tool should shorten the amount of time taken to find and understand relevant microgravity combustion research from days to minutes.

Benefits include:

  • Quick access to relevant NASA combustion research.
  • Better visibility into the experimental evidence.
  • Easier comparisons of combustion behaviour across different atmospheric conditions.
  • Highlighting gaps in research.
  • Investigate spacecraft fire safety scenarios with evidence.

6. Limitations and Intended Use

This tool was developed as a research and decision support tool. It is not a certified fire detection system for spacecraft, flight safety system or a substitute for NASA engineering.

The results should only be used for research purposes. Safety decisions need to be independently verified and further testing completed.
